findings.title: Call to zero-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not compile
findings.body: UsernameForm.java line 47 calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments. The only definition in the superclass UsernamePasswordForm takes a UserModel argument: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user). There is no zero-arg overload in the changed files, so the module does not compile and the whole PR cannot be built or merged.

findings.title: Conditional passkeys disabled for initial userless login
findings.body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) returns webauthnAuth != null && isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null. Both call sites in UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate and UsernamePasswordForm.challenge now only call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm when this returns true, i.e. only when context.getUser() != null. The old code filled the form when the user was null to enable usernameless discoverable-key login with conditional UI autofill. After the change the first login page and its error page never get a WebAuthn challenge or conditional-UI flag, so passkey autofill on initial login is broken.

findings.title: Re-auth forces username form for all users when passkeys enabled
findings.body: Once fixed to pass the user, the guard context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(...) is true for any non-null user whenever the realm has passkeys enabled, because isConditionalPasskeysEnabled only checks feature flag, realm policy and user != null, not whether that user has a passkey credential. Password-only users without passkeys who previously skipped the username step on re-authentication via context.success() will now always be shown the username form and forced to re-enter their username.
